title: BAAJA: $50-100 billion in additional transmission payments
subtitle: Illustrative central-to-higher scenarios | October 31, 2026

sections.heading: Additional payments and customer relief
paragraphs: BAAJA could shift roughly $50-100 billion of transmission costs from other electricity customers to data centers in central-to-higher scenarios. Our central estimate is $56 billion for new loads entering in 2027-2056, with collections beginning in 2030. These are additional payments above the modeled baseline, in constant 2026 dollars, without discounting. The range is a rounded scenario illustration, not a confidence interval or a lower and upper bound. [1, 3]

The bill requires embedded AND incremental transmission charges, with incremental receipts credited against the shared revenue requirement. Holding investment and demand fixed, the extra data-center payments reduce what other customers must pay by the same amount. [1]

sections.heading: Assumptions and range
paragraphs: Demand reaches LBNL's 649 TWh in 2030, then grows at our assumed 3% annually through 2040 and 1.5% thereafter. We assume 80% load factor, 75% coverage, $650,000/MW of assigned network upgrades, 1% annual real construction-cost growth, and 35% of capital already funded by data centers. Capital recovery uses 40 years and 5% real financing, plus 1.5% annual operating costs. Embedded charges use PJM zonal tariffs and a $95,100/MW-year national starting proxy. The cost, coverage and funding shares are judgments, not measured national averages. [2-4]

The approximately $50 billion case assumes 50% prior capital funding ($47 billion calculated). The approximately $100 billion case combines a faster demand path with $750,000/MW of upgrades ($103 billion calculated). Lower outcomes remain plausible: restricting the policy to entrants from 2030 gives $35 billion; $300,000/MW upgrades give $26 billion. Each changes only the stated central assumptions. [3]

sections.heading: Comparison with the transmission ITC
paragraphs: JCT scored the House-passed 2021 Build Back Better transmission investment tax credit at $11.279 billion over FY2022-2031. For a 30-year scale comparison, we normalize its annual amounts using an assumed 2.5% inflation rate and repeat that real ten-year profile three times: approximately $32 billion in 2026 dollars. This is our illustration, not an official 30-year JCT score or a forecast of a continuing program. [3, 5]

The $50-100 billion BAAJA range is approximately 1.6-3.2 times that ITC illustration; the central case is 1.8 times. This compares data-center-funded customer relief with federal budget cost, not equivalent electricity-bill savings or economic benefits.

sections.heading: What is above cost of service?
paragraphs: The central case also exceeds the larger of ordinary payments and incremental service cost by $55.6 billion. That is not a finding of overpayment above fully allocated cost. The larger $145 billion above incremental cost alone includes $89 billion already paid under the modeled baseline. The policy comparison therefore uses additional payments, not that larger total. [3]
